items.text: The Pulumi `protect` resource option is a Pulumi-engine construct enforced entirely within Pulumi.
The Pulumi `protect` resource option is never sent to the cloud provider.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance carries its own `deletionProtection` deletion-protection attribute.
An AWS RDS instance carries its own `deletionProtection` deletion-protection attribute.
Cloud-resource deletion-protection attributes such as `deletionProtection` on GCP Cloud SQL / AWS RDS are enforced by the cloud provider independently of anything Pulumi knows about.

A resource can be unprotected in Pulumi (no `protect` option) and still refuse to delete because of a cloud-side deletion-protection attribute, and vice versa (protected in Pulumi with no cloud-side guard).

The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section with anchor #deletion-protection-on-the-resource-itself explaining how to tell Pulumi `protect` apart from cloud-side deletion protection and resolve each.
The Pulumi `protect` resource option guards a resource within Pulumi (at the engine level).
A GCP Cloud SQL instance carries a separate `deletionProtection` deletion-protection attribute.
An AWS RDS instance carries a separate `deletionProtection` deletion-protection attribute.
Cloud-resource deletion-protection attributes are enforced by the Pulumi provider or the cloud API independently of the Pulumi `protect` option.
The Pulumi `protect` option and cloud-side deletion-protection attributes are complementary layers rather than substitutes for one another.

The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section with anchor #deletion-protection-on-the-resource-itself explaining how to tell the two protection layers apart and resolve a destroy failure caused by either.
A `pulumi destroy` failure is often not a Pulumi engine problem but the resource itself being guarded against deletion.
Three distinct layers can hold deletion protection that blocks `pulumi destroy`: Pulumi's `protect` option, a provider-enforced flag, and a cloud-API-enforced protection.
When `pulumi destroy` fails because a resource is guarded against deletion, the error message usually indicates which of the three protection layers was hit.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option is an engine-level guard that never reaches the cloud provider.
When `pulumi destroy` fails because of the `protect` resource option, the error names the resource URN and mentions `protect`.
The page /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/protect/ exists and explains how to remove the `protect` option.

Some Pulumi providers refuse to issue the delete call at all when a resource carries a deletion-protection attribute, so the failure surfaces from the provider before any request reaches the cloud API.
The `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` resource in `pulumi/pulumi-gcp` has a `deletionProtection` attribute.
The `deletionProtection` attribute on `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` is provider-enforced: the GCP Pulumi provider refuses to delete the instance when it is set, before any request reaches the GCP API.
The `gcp.container.Cluster` resource in `pulumi/pulumi-gcp` has a `deletionProtection` attribute.
The `deletionProtection` attribute on `gcp.container.Cluster` is provider-enforced: the GCP Pulumi provider refuses to delete the cluster when it is set, before any request reaches the GCP API.
Some clouds reject the delete call themselves via their API, independent of Pulumi, when a cloud-side deletion protection is set; the error text in this case comes back from the cloud provider's API.
The `aws.rds.Instance` resource in `pulumi/pulumi-aws` has a `deletionProtection` attribute.
The `aws.rds.Cluster` resource in `pulumi/pulumi-aws` has a `deletionProtection` attribute.
AWS RDS `deletionProtection` (on `aws.rds.Instance` / `aws.rds.Cluster`) is enforced by the AWS API, which rejects the delete call itself rather than the Pulumi provider blocking it.
The `deletionProtection` attribute on `aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` defaults to `false`.
The `aws.ec2.Instance` resource in `pulumi/pulumi-aws` has a `disableApiTermination` attribute.
EC2 `disableApiTermination` on `aws.ec2.Instance` is enforced by the AWS API (EC2 termination protection), which rejects the terminate call independent of Pulumi.
An Azure Resource Manager management lock causes Azure to reject a delete call itself, independent of Pulumi.
When Azure Resource Manager rejects a delete because of a management lock, the API error carries the distinct error code `ScopeLocked`.
The remediation for a provider-enforced deletion-protection flag and for a cloud-API-enforced deletion protection is the same (disable the attribute, `pulumi up`, then `pulumi destroy`).
`pulumi destroy` deletes what is recorded in the stack's state, not what the program currently says.
Setting a resource's deletion-protection attribute to `false` in the Pulumi program alone (without running `pulumi up`) is not enough to let `pulumi destroy` succeed.
Running `pulumi up` after setting a deletion-protection attribute to `false` propagates the change to both the live cloud resource and Pulumi's stack state.
If deletion protection was already disabled outside of Pulumi (e.g., in the cloud console), `pulumi refresh` synchronizes the stack's state with the live resource.
After `pulumi refresh` picks up deletion protection that was disabled outside of Pulumi, `pulumi destroy` succeeds without an intervening `pulumi up`.

The resources listed in the deletion-protection table (GCP Cloud SQL, GKE, BigQuery, AWS RDS, S3, EC2, DynamoDB, Azure locks, Key Vault) are common sources of `pulumi destroy` failures caused by resource-level deletion protection.
The `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` resource has a nested `settings.deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute.

The nested `settings.deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute on `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` guards the instance against deletion at the GCP API level (as distinct from the provider-enforced top-level `deletionProtection`).
The `gcp.bigquery.Table` resource in `pulumi/pulumi-gcp` has a `deletionProtection` attribute.
The `deletionProtection` attribute on `gcp.bigquery.Table` is provider-enforced: the GCP Pulumi provider refuses the delete when it is set.
The `gcp.bigquery.Dataset` resource in `pulumi/pulumi-gcp` has a `deleteContentsOnDestroy` attribute.
Destroying a `gcp.bigquery.Dataset` that still contains tables fails unless `deleteContentsOnDestroy` is `true`.
The `aws.s3.BucketV2` resource in `pulumi/pulumi-aws` has a `forceDestroy` attribute.
The `forceDestroy` attribute on `aws.s3.BucketV2` defaults to `false`.
Deleting a non-empty `aws.s3.BucketV2` fails unless `forceDestroy` is `true`.
The `aws.dynamodb.Table` resource in `pulumi/pulumi-aws` has a `deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute.
The `deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute on `aws.dynamodb.Table` is enforced by the AWS API (the API rejects the delete when it is set).
The `deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute on `aws.dynamodb.Table` defaults to `false`.
The `pulumi/pulumi-azure-native` provider has a `azure-native.authorization.ManagementLockByScope` resource.
The `pulumi/pulumi-azure-native` provider has scope-specific management-lock resource variants, including `azure-native.authorization.ManagementLockAtResourceLevel`.

An Azure management lock of type `CanNotDelete` must be removed before the locked resource can be deleted, independent of anything in the Pulumi program; the lock is enforced by Azure Resource Manager.
`azure-native.keyvault.Vault` (Azure Key Vault) supports soft delete and purge protection.
Destroying an `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` only soft-deletes the vault rather than permanently removing it.
Recreating an Azure Key Vault with the same name as a soft-deleted vault fails with the error `VaultAlreadyExists` until the soft-deleted vault is purged or recovered.
Azure Key Vault purge protection prevents purging a soft-deleted vault until its retention period elapses.
